paragraphs: R' Yaakov son of Ada son of Atalya.
He is mentioned in the Yerushalmi, Gittin chapter 1, halakhah 2: he said in the name of R' Elazar — and R' Zeira was looking at him.[^1]

notes.text: פ״א ה״ב gives 1h 2 explicitly in Jerusalem Talmud, without a new passage check. Both generations Ada and Atalya remain intact, with no titles added to them. The headed Yaakov is the natural implicit reporter and referent of him, but the source does not state the gaze’s reason or tone; no rebuke, scrutiny or motivation is added. All three personal-title abbreviations remain R'.
